correctness.rationale: For strictly positive triples, F(ix)=P(-x^2)+ixQ(-x^2) has argument sum of n strictly increasing angles from 0 to n*pi, hence zeros of P and Q strictly alternate along the negative axis in oriented order. Normalized P and Q are Poisson-binomial with Bernoulli parameters u_1>v_1>u_2>...>v_(n-1)>u_n. Coupling aligned Bernoulli coordinates proves K=O-1/2 <=st E <=st K+1. A common-quantile coupling gives 0<=E-K<=1, so |E-O|=1/2 a.s. Lower bound follows from disjoint integer and half-integer lattices. Approximation of boundary probabilities and positive parity masses extends the result to zeros. Independently convolved all denominator-three triples up to n=4 and checked all CDF inequalities for 10,330 admissible conditional pairs.

evidence: Broadie–Petkova Theorem 1 proves conditional Poisson-binomial laws and individual mean bounds plus modal comparisons, not the paired stochastic ordering or sharp Wasserstein identity. Prior repository result on sharp modal alignment in exactly the same model proves |m_E-m_O|<=3/2, and 1/2 under positive parameters; it concerns modal points rather than a law-to-law optimal transport. Classic oriented Hermite–Biehler and quantile theorems supply the techniques, and a general oriented interlacing theorem could imply this as a corollary, creating an explicit residual priority risk.
